speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SPS also works with community partners like the Salvation Army to conduct family sessions in prison.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: During these sessions, family members are allowed to enter the Prison to spend time with the inmates, and they are designed to encourage bonding between inmates and their children, and they serve as powerful reminders to inmates that they need to turn their lives around.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These family sessions are also held during special occasions, such as Mothers' Day, Fathers' Day and Children's Day.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Other than helping the inmate, SPS also helps their families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Can I proceed to finish up my answer?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Besides family support, employment is another critical factor for successful reintegration.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Employment provides the ex-offenders with a sense of purpose and income to help meet their families' needs.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE), its partners and employers play key roles by providing training and job opportunities for inmates.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Leon Perera asked about skills training for offenders during and after incarceration.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Courses include the Certified Operations Professional training where inmates are trained to be operations professionals in the manufacturing industry or technical supervisors in other industries.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Completing these courses also helps inmates to pursue WSQ Diploma courses upon their release.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: These skills will help inmates to be more competitive when they join the workforce upon their release.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: SPS and SCORE work together with agencies, such as Workforce Singapore, to fund these courses for inmates.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Inmates can use their SkillsFuture credits during their stay at halfway houses or after their release.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And SCORE informs inmates about SkillsFuture programmes and works with halfway house operators to encourage residents to attend courses.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Through the multiple rehabilitation programmes, we help inmates and their family cope with their difficult situation.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about our partnerships with Malay/Muslim organisations to tackle offending, re-offending and drug abuse.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: (In Malay):   MHA has formed close partnerships with the Malay/Muslim community to tackle the issue of offending and re-offending.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have achieved good progress in recent years.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I am encouraged by the progress made by our Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The strong support of our Malay/Muslim volunteers is invaluable in helping our ex-offenders start afresh.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Many people from our community have stepped forward to play a role in supporting the rehabilitation and reintegration efforts of offenders and repeat offenders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: For example, SPS is working closely with the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP) on a rehabilitation programme for Muslim offenders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This includes religious, family and financial literacy programmes during their incarceration, as well as case management and family support services after they are released.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MHA is also partnering the Singapore Muslim Women's Association (PPIS) to enhance drug prevention education efforts within the community.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Under this initiative, PPIS will help spread the anti-drug message to their clients who are participating in their support programmes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: PERGAS (Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association), also shared our concern over drug offending.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Recently, they met and counselled young drug offenders during the pilot run of the Insan Mukmin programme.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: PERGAS is very concerned that our youths lack awareness about the danger of drugs and how drug abuse runs counter to the teachings of Islam.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: They shared with me that they planned to organise a campaign to raise more awareness on this front.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: (In English): Mdm Chair, to conclude, the Home Team is committed to achieve a drug-free Singapore and will increase our efforts to rehabilitate and reintegrate ex-offenders and will partner the community to safeguard the safety and security of Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police will interact and speak with a wide variety of people in coming to their conclusion.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Ultimately, the Police will be guided by advice from the Attorney-General's Chambers, taking into account the facts, the videos which are available and a proper translation of what was said.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share more on how we can support older Home Team officers?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Also, how would the Home Team train to arrive at that strong joint Home Team capabilities that are needed to fight crimes of the future?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These will enable them to have the necessary skills to transit smoothly into a second career.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The departments are also actively looking out for opportunities to deploy and re-employ our veteran officers in both uniformed and civilian positions where we can tap on their experience, skills and knowledge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member also asked about how we can have a better joint Home Team psyche for our officers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In today's complex operating environment, this is critical because no Home Team department completely operates in silo.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In more complex situations, our officers often have to find themselves having to work together on the ground at the operational level.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I spoke earlier about the Police Operations Command Centre, where you will have other Home Team agencies in that nerve cell.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With quicker sharing of information, it will begin to translate into a fuller, whole-of-Home Team operational stance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Officers will learn about the functions of Home Team departments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They will gain a better insight into the heritage, history, ethos and values of each department, as well as the importance of integration across the Home Team departments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As an officer progresses through his career, he will be trained in joint operations and gain an understanding of the different capabilities of the Home Team departments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we have courses like the Home Team Leadership Programmes for Senior and Junior Officers, and the Home Team Senior Command and Staff Course, which will equip officers at different stages of their career with the knowledge, skills and network to work together as one Home Team.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I just wanted to ask the Minister, as it was announced earlier, Police Officers will transit from revolvers to pistols.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I just want to clarify whether the issuance of pistols and use of pistols will be extended to APOs as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For now, we are looking at our own officers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In my cut, I did ask whether the Government had considered issuing non-lethal weapons, for example, to APOs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I wonder the Senior Minister of State could respond to that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I had explained earlier that whenever you give arms to any person, regardless of his background, there will always be these risks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In determining whether to arm an APO, you would look both at the risk assessment as well as the operational needs of the officer and the position in which he has been posted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, I think we need to look at it from that perspective and try to address the risk upstream through proper selection and training.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I just want to clarify for the surveillance cameras which have been installed and also still going on.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I understand that quite a lot of them are recording and re-recording.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Will they be shown online if it is "live" recording?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, for an effective system, what you need is a surveillance of the risk areas and artificial intelligence which then analyses it in real-time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This will allow the Police to form an assessment of an incident and react effectively in real-time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, you will want to go further to use big data to conduct predictive analysis, so that you can intervene even before something happens.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I appreciate what he has said about risk assessment.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But I do not think my question has been answered about whether the Government has actually assessed whether it is feasible to issue APOs, for example, with stun guns.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I think the Singapore Police Force actually has that issued to some officers, but I do not know whether that has been considered for APOs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I just wanted to know yes or no.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will take this back and check with the Police.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I just want to get a confirmation as well as affirmation from the Minister whether MUIS and PERGAS will be consulted, because I believe that MUIS and PERGAS will be able to provide a more accurate interpretation of the imam's text, since he is said to be quoting from verses in the Quran.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I ask the Member whether he thinks that it is alright to quote from a text and encourage violence against others?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is not the question I asked, and I did not refer to the Quran.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Do you think it is alright for someone to refer to any holy text to encourage violence, either by quoting directly or speaking, encouraging such violence?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is the question the Police will be considering.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, do you wish to redraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Behind the scenes, many uniformed and non-uniformed Home Team officers keep us safe and we have much to thank them for.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I enjoin all Singaporeans to work with them in our battle against those who seek to do us harm.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, this leaves me to thank the Home Team on behalf of the House, and I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
